scope: 52 of 87 quantitative records traced to the published Table S2; 35 additional records retain supplied citations, with the Shibata row independently checked. Not a complete certification of every primary measurement.

principal.definition: Correct original CSV row 5 latitude to 34.5 N and row 8 longitude to 146 E from Yamamoto & Kanamatsu (2001), p.56 and coring-location maps. Preserve 7 and 6 cm confirmed by Yamamoto & Aoki (2002), Tables 1/2, p.31 and correlations p.32. Encode CSV 43 upper 10 cm; CSV 52 lower 3 cm; CSV 53 lower 6.7 cm following Table S2, retaining the primary-paper 6.5–7 cm conflict; CSV 55 lower 7 cm as a preservation sensitivity. Keep all other quantitative records and the six excluded pseudo rows. Fill S2 source references without changing row order.

source_conflict: CSV row 53 uses the compilation >6.7 cm interpretation in this conditional reference scenario. Danhara et al. (2010), Table 4 instead gives 6.5–7 cm. Neither version has been established as uniquely correct; endpoint and retained-point alternatives are published separately.
preservation_assumption: CSV row 55 lower 7 cm assumes erosion did not increase thickness through redeposition.
coordinate_datum: Source datums differ according to S2 H76; no unsupported datum conversion was made.
marine_observation_scope: A core thickness is not automatically an atmospheric fallout loading. No current-transport correction is inferred from the Kuroshio hypothesis.
pseudo_rows: Original CSV rows 89–94 retained for traceability but ignored by every active method. No detection threshold, zero or 0.5 cm value invented for S2 unquantified occurrences.
original_csv_row_identity: One-based physical row including header; row order preserved.
